Alex: Heads-up — customer reported failures restoring snapshots after we rotated per-tenant CMKs during maintenance. Need quick triage.
Samira: Which tenant? Any logs or error codes?
Alex: Tenant acct-742. Errors show AccessDenied on S3 GetObject and EBS snapshot copy. KMS Decrypt failing with IncorrectKeyException.
Alex: ```
Error: KMS:Decrypt failed: IncorrectKeyId
  at restore-snapshot (restore_service.go:142)
  cause: CMK arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/old-key-id is disabled
```
Mike: That stack looks like the old CMK got disabled after rotation. Our envelope encryption stores data keys encrypted by tenant CMK so disables break old restores.
Samira: Right — rotation should generate new data keys for future backups, but existing snapshots still reference the old CMK. If you disable or change the key policy on the old CMK, restores will fail.
Emma: Who disabled the old key? Audit?
Alex: Oncall job by Jerry ran the rotation and then cleanup. I see a CloudTrail record: `kms:DisableKey` at 1769989805 tied to key/old-key-id and user jerry@redwood.
Jerry: Yup — I ran the cleanup script to disable the previous key after rotation. Thought that was standard. Didn't realize active snapshots could still need it. Sorry about that. :grimacing:
Samira: Quick recovery options: (1) re-enable the old CMK (fastest), (2) if you have archived data keys in the backup manifest, rewrap them with the new CMK, (3) restore from a copy that was re-encrypted. Fastest is re-enable.
Emma: Security prefers controlled enable with approval + audit trail. We should avoid blanket RBAC changes. Propose temporary RBAC exception: allow infra-runbook role to call `kms:EnableKey` for `key/old-key-id` for 1 hour, with MFA + sec-eng approval.
Mike: Long-term fix: update rotation runbook to leave previous CMKs Enabled for N days or until snapshot inventory confirms no references. Also add an automated check to fail rotation if snapshots still reference the old key.
Samira: I'll create AWS Config rule + CloudWatch alarm to detect `kms:DisableKey` on keys referenced by snapshots. Also will add a snapshot tag `snapshot.encryption_key_id` during backup and persist key-id in the backup manifest. That will make detection/searching easier.
Alex: Action items: 1) Jerry to re-enable old key now or request RBAC escalation; 2) Samira to add alert + config rule; 3) Mike to update rotation runbook and gating; 4) Emma to document approval flow and record incident. I'll open an incident ticket. :thumbsup:
sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-321 created and channel #inc-1769991234 provisioned.
Jerry: I re-enabled the key at 1769991500 and triggered a restore test — customer confirms success. Sorry again; will follow the new checklist next time. :pray:
Alex: Good recovery. For follow-up: run vuln triage to detect snapshots with missing encryption metadata or keys that were disabled unexpectedly. Not a CVE, but process failure — still need a postmortem.
Samira: On it. I'll add a detection rule for untagged snapshots and a CloudTrail query for `kms:DisableKey` events tied to snapshot key IDs. Will open PR for runbook changes by EOD.
Mike: Also suggest adding a pre-rotation dry-run that queries snapshot index and fails if any snapshot points at the key-to-be-disabled.
Emma: Thanks all — once PRs land let's coordinate a quick all-hands email to infra and backup owners so this doesn't repeat.
Alex: Closing loop for now, will attach logs and the CloudTrail link to the incident ticket.
Samira: PR link to follow in the ticket.
